subject.title: [Bug]: Windows gateway listens but local health/status time out after Telegram polling stall (v2026.5.20)

question: Should OpenClaw add supervisor/process-level escalation for repeated channel or Gateway liveness failures here, or wait for affected-host proof that identifies a narrower Telegram, session, or Gateway owner boundary?
rationale: Source inspection shows several mitigations but not a proven fix for the alive-listening health/status timeout, and changing recovery from in-process retries to process exits affects operator behavior across platforms.

options.title: Require affected-host proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask for a current-main Windows Telegram run with status, health, logs, provider/tool context, and plain Telegram API proof before choosing the fix layer.

options.title: Sponsor supervisor escalation
options.body: A maintainer can decide that repeated failed channel recovery should intentionally exit the Gateway under supported supervisors, with upgrade notes and platform proof.

options.title: Split narrower trackers
options.body: If new proof separates Telegram send loss, Gateway RPC liveness, and session recovery, split the remaining work into those owner-specific issues and close this umbrella later.

recommendation.title: Require affected-host proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask for a current-main Windows Telegram run with status, health, logs, provider/tool context, and plain Telegram API proof before choosing the fix layer.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision is cross-cutting Gateway recovery policy, and steipete appears repeatedly in the Gateway health-monitor/lifecycle history.
